fields.description:
After beating Cataclysm i got really hyped about the cape section and decided that i wanted more so i went further in cape mechanics and built this hack, this hack is the ultimate cape challenge a full pit hack featuring a lot of cape tricks since normal flight till the most deep pit of cape glitches.

This is a challenge made by me for myself, so we have 3 endings, if you don't wanna play the entire hack you can go for an any% run and for those who wanna a real challenge you can go for 100%, this is the first pit hack where you can decide your route, so open lunar magic, see all rooms, route your path and go for the TAS.

14 cape rooms, 3 bosses, some secrets and some extra challenges!

Hope you enjoy it and let's have fun!

Fixes 1.1
- 3 moons had problems so i fixed
- added a big door in room 102 to avoid useless damage boost
- added credits for the first 100% blind clear

fields.description:
Well, after a long time, The Pit Level 3 has been completed.

This hack was started in 2015 and I worked hard on it until mid-2017. For personal reasons, I was forced to interrupt progress and it was practically stopped until 2022. From 2022 onwards I managed to work hard on it again and finish it.

The focus of this hack was not difficulty, although it is somewhat complex. My goal was to make a fun hack. Because it was mostly made between 2015 and 2017, this hack is made up of many shelljumps, yumps, keyjumps and things like that. Nowadays, that's not as cool as it was in 2015, but I didn't have much of a choice. I managed to change many rooms and eliminate some repeated shelljumps, but overall if I were to change everything, I would have to do a new hack.

FULL HACK VIDEO: https://youtu.be/mrlO3VQiz9U

Anyway, that was the most I could do. Although this hack is full of shelljumps/keyjumps, it also has some cool tricks, as you will see in some rooms.

NOTE: The water room (room 112) is different from what appears in the video. I changed it because it was generating a lot of lag, but unfortunately I couldn't change it in the video, as the TAS was desyncing.

NOTE 2: The crash at the end of the video was for pure fun, it is not mandatory. The hack ends as soon as you kill the boss.

That's it, download and enjoy!

fields.description:
This is a romhack I began developing quite some time ago, and after a long stretch of on-and-off work, I'm finally getting around to completing it. It used to be said that my hack would be released around the same time as Mario Maker 3, so I'm happy to be releasing it ahead of schedule!

The central focus is on building unique challenges through custom ASM. I wrote many original sprites, blocks, mechanics, and gimmicks with each level typically revolving around one particular ASM creation. The design blends standard and kaizo elements, but generally offers freedom in how to approach obstacles, rather than forcing a single strict approach.

While the early levels are fairly approachable, the difficulty ramps up significantly as the hack progresses. Later stages present intense challenges, even for the best players, demanding skill much deeper than just raw execution. Progress may seem slow at times, but those who stick with it will hopefully find steady improvement, and a rewarding experience as proficiency grows, perception sharpens, and difficulty gives way to hard-earned intuition.

fields.description:
What started as a small idea for a “classic-style” Kaizo hack slowly turned into a personal revenge project — inspired by my time playing Responsible World.
But let’s be real: this isn’t about revenge (well… maybe a little). It’s more about seeing if I could still create something fresh in a scene where it feels like everything has already been done.

The result?
22 exits full of pain, frustration, and a complete disregard for your time. If you’re into old-school difficulty, this one’s for you.

Features:

No QoL patches (except for the framerule fix)

Kaizo blocks. Lots of them.

Checkpoints that don’t save (1-Ups, Dragon Coins — you know the drill)

Pure, unapologetic difficulty

Zero respect for human sanity

You’ve been warned.

Good luck.



Much thanks and appreciation towards the people helping me out shaping this project into what it is.


update 1.01: Fixed random crashes on the super NT

fields.description:
You exit from your last-played level victorious. The design was fine, if not familiar, but engaging and fun. You jumped over the pits, you avoided the munchers, and touching the goal tape felt satisfying enough. The gimmicks were really neat, and some of the more unique elements ignited your imagination about the yet unplayed levels that await on the road ahead. What new obstacles would the creator expect you to overcome? As you ponder this, traversing the overworld of the hack you are currently playing, you see a streak of green and yellow flash across the sky. Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it’s a caped union plumber indulging in aerodynamic equestrianism! At first they look ridiculous and awkward. It doesn’t even look fun, but, you can’t stop watching. How are they even doing that? It looks hard, but also kind of interesting. Their horse doesn’t even have wings! Why does it keep sticking its tongue out?! You think to yourself, “Could I do it too?” A disembodied voice whispers back into your thoughts, “You can, if you try.”

Chinese astrology says the Year of the Horse is upon us! This first of its kind Yoshi horse flight hack comes as an unlikely collaboration between 4 joint 2006 Time Magazine ‘Person of the Year’ award recipients. The premise is simple, in every level you must eat the 5 golden berries and then hatch and collect your prize. The path to credits has 9 levels, and there are 4 bonus levels after the credits that include 3 guest levels. This hack is not a tutorial. It is a challenge that tests your understanding and consistency of control, and allows you to improve as you go. There is a simple practice level within the hack that provides a space to work on your horse and horseless flight fundamentals freely.

Good luck, and safe flying. We believe in you.

fields.description:
The Age of Filebin Hacks has been a cultural movement that emerged in recent years, with various authors releasing certain hacks to their filebins instead of submitting them to the hacks section. Reasons for keeping their works out of the public eye may vary from author to author, be it fear of potential notoriety, avoiding unwanted commentary, or creating something too self-indulgent for general audiences. With filebin releases having less eyes on them, authors were more inclined to release hacks that were experimental or raw — at least when compared to public works — without fear of harsh judgement or needless criticism. Nevertheless, there have been a number of notable filebin hacks over the years that still managed to reach many people by word-of-mouth.

As of recent, it seems that a few brave creators — authors who pioneered the Age of Filebin Hacks — have sacrificed notable works from their respective filebins to the hacks section, thereby bringing forth the beginning of the end. And so I, in solidarity, will also do my part. Let us put to rest this age of old, without need of any dusty old 'bin to express ourselves. On this page, I present this offering of mine: ...10yumps.

...so, anyway...

Originally released in my filebin at the start of 2023, 10yumps was simply a collection of silly consistency challenges, or just dumb levels, that I made for some friends — I even made a dull sequel to it a year later. This new version is a curated consolidation of both hacks, with barely any changes to the levels themselves.

For those that played and enjoyed the originals: I appreciate you, even if you have poor taste in hacks.

If you’re unfamiliar with the hack and happen to be interested in it: Difficulty from level to level can vary wildly. Good luck, and I’m (not really) sorry.

That said, I hope you have fun.

fields.description:
Riding on the wave of newly-liberated filebin hacks, here's something I put out a year ago that, as far as I know, no one's had the guts to beat yet. So, to any completionists out there, consider this submission a formal triple-dog dare. It should be identical to the file version.

This is the Big Sprawling Input Block Olympus level I wasn’t experienced enough to make in 2022, the third and final incarnation of the idea first seen in the Trans Liberation demo. It’s comprised of 4 sections of some returning setups from the Trans Liberation versions and some newer ones, incorporating all 7 block types (A, B, X/Y, LEFT, RIGHT, and the widely beloved UP and DOWN). It doesn’t explore every facet of the gimmick’s potential (you can find a much more extensive use in Eden’s The Possibility of an Island), but it will still probably make you play in ways you never have before.

Reviews of the original material speak for themselves:
“I’m sadly not smart enough” -Eden
“This is a brain-bender” -GlitchCat
“This is the most mindfucked thing I have ever played” -Lungfish
“Holy mother of god this might be the hardest level I’ve ever cleared” -Revolug
“Well this seems about as hard as trans liberation so appropriate” -Maddy
“This is some bottom of the SMW iceberg shit” -Jonah
“I’m sending the SMWC admins to your house” -Mason
“You are one sick motherfucker” -Le4che

This is definitely the most extreme level I have ever made or will ever make. After this and Safespace Challenge, I lost all appetite for exploring ultra-high tightness/density, as I feel I was flying too close to the sun. I barely even recognize this as my own anymore, but I still think it's good and at least worth playing with tools. Proceed with caution either way.

Level ASM by ShadowMistressYuko; music porting by Jonah and Fyre.

fields.description:
Welcome to Super BanzaiChuck World, an ambitious Kaizo journey dedicated to the German YouTuber and streamer BanzaiChuck to simply say thank you for his constantly committed and high-quality entertainment, with which he makes many people a little happier in their lives.
You are a little Bonzai (-chuck) who sets out into the wide world to follow the Way Of The Banzai and thereby become a True BanzaiChuck.
But to walk this path you have to surpass yourself, because it is physical perfection balanced with sublime genius that a True BanzaiChuck strives for.
Each level is another step on your journey, specializing in a particular gimmick/mechanic or special sprites/blocks. At the beginning you have the choice of either entering a small tutorial section to learn the respective level topic and special mechanics, or diving straight into the level and putting your skills to the test.
Are you ready to walk this path and become a True BanzaiChuck?


Super BanzaiChuck World features:

- a challenging but fair Kaizo journey
--> length: 20 exits, some with several subsections
--> difficulty: some parts are in the intermediate range while some things also reach into the low Kaizo expert range)
- typical QoL features (retry, autosave, ...)
- optional tutorials and custom music
- a semi-open overworld
- 4 switch palaces that unlock the further path of the Banzai
- 2 custom bosses
- a bonus mini-game that is unlocked after completing the hack
- 3 hidden scrolls containing clues to a secret area (for all explorers and completionists)

PS: Don't judge a creator by their first hack (my first attempt really wasn't a great job!)

PPS: To get a better impression you can watch the playthrough of BanzaiChuck (V1.0) here:
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLowCpocefzgxCwiA6eBIPzpf2DDYWV5ik

V1.1 (02/2026)
- a handful of smaller adjustments and modifications
- ability to reset checkpoints
- partially removed the BanzaiChuck personalized part of the hack (Bonus Area) and incorporated it into the hack elsewhere

raw_fields.description:
Welcome to Super BanzaiChuck World, an ambitious Kaizo journey dedicated to the German YouTuber and streamer BanzaiChuck to simply say thank you for his constantly committed and high-quality entertainment, with which he makes many people a little happier in their lives.
You are a little Bonzai (-chuck) who sets out into the wide world to follow the Way Of The Banzai and thereby become a True BanzaiChuck.
But to walk this path you have to surpass yourself, because it is physical perfection balanced with sublime genius that a True BanzaiChuck strives for.
Each level is another step on your journey, specializing in a particular gimmick/mechanic or special sprites/blocks. At the beginning you have the choice of either entering a small tutorial section to learn the respective level topic and special mechanics, or diving straight into the level and putting your skills to the test.
Are you ready to walk this path and become a True BanzaiChuck?


Super BanzaiChuck World features:

- a challenging but fair Kaizo journey 
  --> length: 20 exits, some with several subsections 
  --> difficulty: some parts are in the intermediate range while some things also reach into the low Kaizo expert range)
- typical QoL features (retry, autosave, ...) 
- optional tutorials and custom music
- a semi-open overworld  
- 4 switch palaces that unlock the further path of the Banzai
- 2 custom bosses
- a bonus mini-game that is unlocked after completing the hack
- 3 hidden scrolls containing clues to a secret area (for all explorers and completionists)

[i]PS: Don't judge a creator by their first hack (my first attempt really wasn't a great job!)

PPS: To get a better impression you can watch the playthrough of BanzaiChuck (V1.0) here:[/i]

fields.description:
Welcome to Hage World 2!

Baldio smells something nasty coming from the castle in the distance and a pink slime seems to be covering the structure. Baldio must jump, duck, spin, fly, and murder his way through the land to put an end to the foul stench.

This hack has two possible paths for you to take to get to the final castle, but those who want all the exits, secrets, and fun will be rewarded for traveling both.

There is an additional set of special world levels that are a bit beyond the difficulty of the base game for you to pit yourself against! None of the special world levels count as exits, but there are secrets hidden within.

Folks who don't like to scratch that puzzle itch even mildly can use the attached hint sheet instead of poking through the puzzle. ( The puzzle is not meant to be too difficult though so I hope everyone gives it a fair shake)

(Editors note, Hage means Bald)

fields.description:
Warning: If you played "ESCAPE FROM LA PLUME" the music and visuals will be very similar, the gameplay couldn´t be any different though :)

An idea born from a funny bug in "ESCAPE FROM LA PLUME" inspired me to turn this beginner experience into a full on yoshiflight hack. Dont be scared off the difficulty rating - yoshiflight is hard and requires knowledge and experience to be mastered. Parity manipulation is not needed, but sure makes life easier in some levels. The difficulty starts rather fair, but will soon ramp up as the obstacles become harder too maneuver and the enemies more fierce. This hack is intended as a good starting point for all cape friends, that want to give our favorite horse a go.

Features:
- Yoshiflight only hack (tongue and tongueless) - none of that running and jumping stuff
- gorgeous Overworld made by Stivi
- beautiful levels with visuals from bonjoursauce
- 11 exits (most on the shorter side)
- friendly shoutout rooms (no progress is lost on entering) with new and old friends

I want to take the time and thank sauce for all his help throughout the process, you pushed me to keep on doing more then I did and offered so much creativity, help and awesomeness
- this hack would not be the same without you. I really think you have outdone yourself with the visuals in the levels and I hope you are as proud of this little funny projected It started half a year ago, as I am.

Big shoutouts to Stivi for making this wonderful Overworld - and for being incredibly patient and helpful for this cool project :)


Enjoy "TaleSpin" and lets hope you never go into tailspin.

Changelog:

V1.1 fixed multiple breaks in "Easy there green one", "Can I haz star", "A foal is born", "Caparison Mansion"

fields.description:
PATHMAKER is a short 5-exit puzzle hack in which you need to MAKE a PATH for Mario. Incredible.

This spawned from a silly idea that I had half a month ago and that Donut happened to have code made for. That code forces Mario to reenact the Titlescreen Movement on command. And I made this little puzzle hack around that premise. Your goal is to clear out the levels in a way that Mario can collect the orb at the end, as he repeats the movements of the titlescreen. This is my first attempt at making a puzzle hack and I had some trouble coming up with fun ideas, which is why this hack ended up on the short side. But all things considered I think I turned this idea into a fun little brainteaser.

For the v1.1 changelog please refer to the readme.

Credits
Graphics, Leveldesign, Idea
by Tob

Major ASM
- Titlescreen movement code by Donut.
- Statusbar by Arinsu

Additional ASM
by Kevin, ASMagician Maks, imamelia, Sonikku

Custom Music
by MercuryPenny, icrawfish, NamyX, MidiGuy, brickblock369, Tamaki, Samantha

Special Thanks to the testers:
bebn legg, Arinsu, You :>
